title: Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra coast between Nellore and Tuni on Friday; IMD issues cyclone alert
dek: The storm stalled overnight 610 km east of Chennai but is forecast to cross the coast around noon on 20 November as a very severe cyclonic storm with winds of up to 145 kmph and a surge of up to 2 metres.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Cyclonic Storm Akvan stayed almost stationary over the Bay of Bengal overnight but is still forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on Friday, 20 November, as a very severe cyclonic storm with sustained winds of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in its bulletin issued at 5.45 am IST on Tuesday. It has raised its warning for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts to a cyclone alert, an orange message, and now warns of a storm surge of up to 2 metres.

The system strengthened into a cyclonic storm and was named Akvan at 5.30 pm on Monday, and the IMD expects it to become a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening and a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning. Heavy rain is forecast over coastal Andhra Pradesh, north Tamil Nadu and Odisha from Wednesday, and at isolated places in Gangetic West Bengal on 19 and 20 November.

## What happened

At 2.30 am IST on Tuesday the storm lay near latitude 12.2°N and longitude 85.7°E, about 610 km east of Chennai, 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha and 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, the bulletin said. It had "remained practically stationary during past 09 hours", with winds of 65-75 kmph gusting to 85 kmph.

The IMD's forecast table shows it moving north-northwest and then northwest, with winds reaching 95-105 kmph by 11.30 pm on Tuesday, 115-125 kmph by 11.30 am on Thursday and 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph from Thursday night, when it is expected to be near 15.2°N, 82.0°E. It is forecast to be just off the central Andhra Pradesh coast, near 15.7°N, 81.0°E, at 11.30 am on Friday, to weaken to a severe cyclonic storm over land by Friday night, and to become a depression by late on Saturday.

IMD Director General Mrityunjay Mohapatra said on Monday that the storm's maximum impact was expected from Thursday night to Friday afternoon, according to reports.

## Storm surge and wind

The bulletin said a storm surge of 1.0 to 2.0 metres above the astronomical tide was very likely to inundate low-lying areas of Prakasam, Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, Konaseema and Kakinada districts at the time of landfall, up from 1.0-1.5 metres in Monday's bulletin, with the peak surge expected over Bapatla, Krishna and West Godavari from Friday morning until the afternoon. A surge of about half a metre is likely along those districts from the early hours to the evening of Friday.

Along and off the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts, it forecast squally winds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph until Tuesday, gales of 60-70 kmph gusting to 80 kmph from Wednesday evening, and 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph from Thursday night until landfall, with "phenomenal" seas from Thursday evening. Squally winds of 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph are forecast along the Odisha coast from Thursday morning and along the north Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coasts on Thursday and Friday. The IMD has advised that people living in coastal huts be moved to safer places.

## Where rain is forecast

The rainfall warnings in the 5.45 am bulletin, by the IMD's dates:

- Coastal Andhra Pradesh: heavy rain at isolated places on 18 November, then heavy to very heavy rain at a few places with isolated extremely heavy falls (21 cm or more) on 19 and 20 November.
- North Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal: heavy rain at isolated places on 17 and 20 November, and heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on 18 and 19 November.
- Odisha: heavy rain at isolated places on 18 November, and heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places from 19 to 21 November.
- Rayalaseema: heavy rain at isolated places on 19 and 20 November.
- Eastern Telangana: heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on 20 November.
- Gangetic West Bengal: light to moderate rain at many places, with heavy rain at isolated places, on 19 and 20 November.
- Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, east Vidarbha and east Madhya Pradesh: heavy rain at isolated places on 20 and 21 November.

## Warnings for fishermen and preparations

Fishermen have been told not to go into the southwest and westcentral Bay of Bengal until 20 November, the southeast and eastcentral Bay until 18 November, and the northwest Bay, the waters off Odisha and West Bengal, on 19 and 20 November.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu held a review meeting at the Secretariat on Monday and directed officials to deploy National and State Disaster Response Force teams in advance, keep energy department staff ready to restore power, and divert floodwater into reservoirs, with round-the-clock monitoring from the state's real-time governance centre, according to reports. Odisha has alerted all 30 of its districts and opened round-the-clock control rooms, and district officials in southern Odisha have ordered the early evacuation of vulnerable people, reports said. In Tamil Nadu, the state's relief commissioner urged people to follow only official bulletins, after private forecasters circulated computer-model forecasts showing a landfall near Chennai; the IMD's track keeps the storm well off the Tamil Nadu coast.

## Background

Akvan is the third cyclone to threaten the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts since late October. Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast in late October, and its remnants caused floods and a landslide in southern Odisha that killed at least three people in Kandhamal district. Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the coast near Ongole on 3 November, damaging crops on more than 30,000 hectares in 15 districts of Andhra Pradesh, according to the state government, though no deaths were reported.

November is one of the most active months for cyclones in the Bay of Bengal, after the south-west monsoon withdraws. The names used in the north Indian Ocean are drawn in sequence from a list contributed by 13 countries in the region; Arnab was proposed by Bangladesh, Murasu by India and Akvan by Iran, according to the published list.

For Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, a third storm in a month would arrive on soil that is already wet and over kharif crops, including paddy, that are close to harvest. Exact effects will depend on where the storm crosses the coast. The IMD's earliest outlooks pointed further north, towards the stretch between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur; its latest bulletin has moved the expected crossing south, to central and south coastal Andhra Pradesh.

## What happens next

The IMD has moved from a pre-cyclone watch to a cyclone alert, the second of its warning stages; if the storm follows the forecast track it is expected to issue a cyclone warning, and then a post-landfall outlook, for the stretch of coast where landfall is expected. The landfall point may still shift; weather models differ on the storm's later movement and strength, according to reports citing the IMD's outlook.

## Key numbers

- 610 km: distance from Chennai at 2.30 am IST on Tuesday
- 670 km: distance from Visakhapatnam
- Around noon, 20 November: forecast landfall between Nellore and Tuni
- 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph: forecast winds at landfall
- 1-2 metres: forecast storm surge in six Andhra Pradesh districts
- 21 cm or more: extremely heavy rain forecast at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh on 19-20 November
